title: Old Windows Aren't Melting #science #physics
description:
Old windows aren't melting. Some old panes are thicker at the bottom, so people say glass is a slow liquid. But at room temperature glass would take far longer than the age of the universe to sag visibly. Old glass was spun (crown glass) or blown (cylinder glass) by hand, so it came out uneven, and glaziers often set the thick edge down. Old panes also exist with the thick edge at the top or the side.

More physics of light and glass: Why is a rainbow always at the same angle? https://youtu.be/CywvAndxdSk

Sources
- Zanotto, E. D. (1998), Do cathedral glasses flow? American Journal of Physics 66: 392–395
- DoITPoMS, University of Cambridge: The glass transition, 'The myth of flowing windows'
- The bars in the animation are not to scale

Have you seen an old window with wavy glass?
